The test image shows a corn stalk broken/snapped at a node. Key features:
- Stalk has snapped at a node joint
- Tiny black specks/dots scattered on the stalk surface
- Shredded, fibrous pith with stringy vascular strands visible
- Dry, tan/brown tissue

This is a **stem** issue. Top candidates: **Charcoal_Stalk_Rot** (tiny black sclerotia on shredded pith), **Diplodia_Stalk_Rot** (small black structures in rind), **Physoderma_Stalk_Rot** (snaps at nodes with black nodes).

Now viewing one reference from each top candidate:

The Diplodia reference (Corn_Disease_14.jpg) is strikingly similar to the test image: broken stalk at a node, same dry field setting, same angle. The test image also shows many tiny black specks on the stalk surface, matching Diplodia's pycnidia embedded in the rind. Let me use the 4th view to confirm with a second Diplodia reference.

This second Diplodia reference confirms the match perfectly. It shows the exact same tiny black dots (pycnidia) embedded in the tan/cream stalk rind near a node, identical to the test image.

**Summary of evidence:**
- Test image: broken stalk at a node, covered in tiny black specks on the tan/cream rind surface
- Diplodia_Stalk_Rot reference 1: broken stalk at node in dry field (same setting/angle)
- Diplodia_Stalk_Rot reference 2: clearly shows small black pycnidia embedded in the stalk rind, tan coloring — exact match
- Charcoal shows internal shredded charred pith (not external specks)
- Physoderma shows dark spots on green stalk (not matching)
